newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 8.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:

* Texaco Inc confirmed a report published Monday in The Wall Street Journal that it was talking with the U.S unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Star Enterprise, a joint venture between Texaco and Saudi Aramco, to form an alliance in refining and marketing operations.
* Computer Associates International Inc made a $1.2 billion cash bid for Cheyenne Software Inc, which makes mass storage software for business computers.
* Motorola Inc reported sharp decline in earnings for the last quarter and warned earnings in the next quarter might be hurt by restructuring charges.
* Quintiles Transnational Corp said it planned to buy Innovex Inc of Britain for $747.5 million in stock.
* Best Products Co said it would close 81 of its 169 stores and lay off 4,500 employees.
* HFS Inc has agreed to buy Resort Condominiums International for about $625 million, $550 million in cash and the remainder in HFS common stock.
* Donald Trump sold his interest in the Grand Hyatt Hotel in New York to Hyatt Corp for $140 million.
* Securities and Exchange Commission has charged a member of the board of the Philadelphia Stock Exchange with cheating customers.
* Investor Mikael Salovaara has resigned from the Blackstone Group, a merchant bank and advisory firm.
* U.S. Supreme Court questioned whether a federal law obliging cable television systems to carry the signals of most broadcast stations was a violation of their right to free speech.

* Falling stock prices have recently eroded the value of several deals in the media and telecommunications industries including Worldcom's takeover of MFS Communications Co Inc and U S West Communications Group's purchase of Continental Cablevision.

* The contrasting personal styles of the presidents of the Canadian Automobile Workers and United Automobile Workers unions are among the many differences between auto industry talks in Canada and the United States.
* U.S. corporations outlays for research and development have fallen this decade, especially in basic research, as they concentrate on developing products for the market.
* U.S. consumer credit rose $3.3 billion in August to $1.16 trillion or 3.5 percent at an annual rate.

* The Dow Jones industrial average topped the 6,000 point level for the first time before closing down on profit taking. The NASDAQ index made its first closing high in four months amid a rally in technology stocks.
